meta.title: Reference Slide Style — Editable Starter Layouts

slides.title:
Insights &
action plan
slides.subtitle: [Audience / customer / business question]
slides.meta:
[Team or point of view]
[Planning horizon / next milestone]
slides.speaker_notes: Replace the gray image placeholder with an approved image behind the white panel. Keep its aspect ratio; crop rather than stretch. Never copy the source wordmark by default.

slides.title: Organize the story around decisions and execution
slides.subtitle: Use three bands to explain the narrative, not to list every individual slide.
slides.takeaway: Keep detailed evidence in notes or an appendix; keep the main story decision-focused.

slides.title: Use six focused cards to frame the opportunity
slides.subtitle: Use this grid for six parallel opportunities, workstreams, roles, or priorities.

slides.title: Compare three options on the same evidence
slides.subtitle: Give each option the same structure: category, name, evidence, and a boundary.
slides.takeaway: State the implication: which option should move forward, and what still needs validation?
slides.source_note: Evidence note: replace with actual source IDs and as-of date. Do not reuse the reference deck’s claims.

slides.title: Connect the workflow to delivery and acceptance
slides.subtitle: Show the user journey above the system, then explain the controls and acceptance criteria.

callouts.title: Customer and budget
callouts.body:
[Who uses the result?]
[Which task and budget does it serve?]

callouts.title: Human decisions
callouts.body:
[What must a person approve?]
[What can be corrected or reversed?]

callouts.title: Quality and efficiency
callouts.body:
[Define the acceptance test.]
[Measure against a stated baseline.]

callouts.title: Owner and continuation gate
callouts.body:
[Name the accountable role.]
[State the evidence needed to proceed.]

slides.source_note: Status note: separate existing capabilities, proposed work, assumptions, and acceptance targets.

slides.title: Use a compact matrix to make evidence comparable
slides.subtitle: Show the sample and its limits; an unknown status is not evidence of absence.
slides.source_note: Sample note: replace all cells with verified data; define denominators, unknowns, and source coverage.

slides.title: Show shared capabilities beneath distinct use cases
slides.subtitle: Clarify what each application owns and what the shared foundation provides.
slides.platform_note: Applications own customer outcomes; shared gaps need an owner, version, and joint test.
slides.io_text:
Inputs: goals, context, permissions, time, and budget
Outputs: status, intervention, artifacts, evidence, cost, and errors
slides.source_note: Architecture note: label current, reusable, adapted, and proposed capabilities separately.

slides.title: Turn a one-off result into a repeatable process
slides.subtitle: Use the cards for stages, the arrows for sequence, and the bottom strip for accountability.
slides.sequence: Task → Baseline → Demo → Evaluation → Trial → Diagnosis → Retest
slides.takeaway: The delivery owner improves the result; the evaluation owner independently verifies the change.

slides.title: Make feedback traceable and improvements testable
slides.subtitle: Separate usability from customer value; connect both to the same task and output version.
slides.input_title: Feedback inputs | the same task run
slides.ledger:
Shared issue log: task ID / run ID / artifact version
Preserve failures, evidence, edits, and feedback

stages.title: Fix & retest
stages.body:
Repeat the task
Add a regression test

slides.return_text: Revisit customer → Validate change → Release / rollback
slides.internal_body:
[Observe task completion, recovery,
and the effort required.]
[Use fixed tasks to reproduce errors.]
slides.external_body:
[Observe repeat use and value.]
[Track real buying signals.]
[Keep dropouts in the denominator.]
slides.source_note: Validation note: replace the placeholders with task-specific evidence and agreed measures.

slides.title: Advance through clear gates, not dates alone
slides.subtitle: Use time windows as planning boundaries; evidence determines whether work should proceed.

cards.label: [WINDOW 1]
cards.title: Scope & baseline
cards.body:
[Confirm the customer]
[Freeze task and inputs]
[Assign the owner]
[Resolve dependencies]

cards.label: [WINDOW 2]
cards.title: Build & verify
cards.body:
[Complete the workflow]
[Test quality and control]
[Track recovery and cost]
[Release a reusable version]

cards.label: [WINDOW 3]
cards.title: Customer value
cards.body:
[Observe sustained use]
[Check buying signals]
[Evaluate unit economics]
[Continue, adjust, or stop]

slides.takeaway: Next: productize proven work → repeat the same task → expand only after the next evidence gate.
slides.source_note: Planning note: time windows and thresholds are placeholders, not inherited commitments.
slides.speaker_notes: For a closing slide, reuse the comparison layout with columns for priorities, required support, and continue / adjust / stop rules.
